item.title: French police officers guilty of Michel Zecler assault: What happens now?
item.description:
Beating of Michel Zecler in 2020 sparked outrage over police brutality after it was caught on security cameras Three French police officers who beat a black music producer they said was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic have been found guilty of intentional, racist violence. The brutal assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, was caught on security cameras in his building in 2020 and triggered outrage in France over police brutality. The trial this month was considered a turning point for the recognition of racist violence. Continue reading...

item.title: Denmark accuses Russia of assassination plot, expels diplomat
item.description:
Denmark has accused Moscow of being behind a failed assassination attempt targeting a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen, further escalating tensions between Europe and Russia. In response, Danish authorities have ordered the expulsion of a Russian diplomat and announced tighter restrictions on visas for Russian tourists. Yuka Royer reports.

item.title: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise
item.description:
Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.

Sources: CBS News, France 24, PBS NewsHour

item.title: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit
item.description:
The UK and the EU signed three agreements on Friday at a summit in Brussels, marking a new effort to reset post-Brexit relations. The deals aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link emissions trading schemes and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit an “obvious failure” to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, a position criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who has warned of a political backlash. Daniel Quinlan has this story.

Sources: BBC News, Flaming Hydra, France 24

item.title: Welcome to Software Beirut
item.description:
Last week, when it briefly looked like the world was collapsing while I sat on the tarmac, I wrote about the arrival of Software Beirut —“where nothing is broken all the time, but anything might break at any time, and the main skill you need is not being surprised.” I’m no Tom Friedman , but many people seemed to enjoy the phrase and encouraged me to keep using it even as outages at the FAA, Chase, and Microsoft proved to be isolated incidents unrelated to bad guys using advanced AI. Well, hold my mustache wax! Because I’m doubling down. The fact that all of the software chaos appears to have had boring causes doesn’t negate my point—it improves it. Software Beirut is not an event but an environment, shaped by three forces that arrived at roughly the same time: AI is exposing vulnerabilities in critical software at unprecedented speed; the rush to fix the bugs creates its own hair ball…

Sources: 404 Media, Flaming Hydra, The Atlantic

item.title: Spain court grants bail to pro-Palestinian activist James ‘Fergie’ Chambers
item.description:
Pro-Palestinian donor James ‘Fergie’ Chambers released as court considers extradition request In a blur of events surrounding the Trump administration’s effort to extradite James “Fergie” Chambers, Spain released the wealthy US activist and donor on bail even as Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner, Stella Schnabel, acting on a request from US authorities. Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza. Continue reading...

item.title: Did you come down with GTA flu? I won’t judge – I may even join you in Vice City | Imogen West-Knights
item.description:
Millions are throwing sickies and no wonder. For gamers who have waited 13 years, this is the equivalent of a football World Cup If there were an unusual number of people missing from your workplace at the back end of this week, they may have come down with GTA flu . You don’t need to be a video game person to have heard that there’s a new instalment of Grand Theft Auto , the enormously popular series in which you drive around sprawling American cities committing crimes.
